title: Generate config and run-monitor schema mirrors
summary: Make Config and RunMonitorRecord the explicit schema authorities, generate their committed consumer artifacts deterministically, and enforce drift checks across local, CI, audit, and release suites.
reason: The Run Monitor pair differed only by consumer metadata while the overlapping config schemas were maintained independently, allowing defaults and validation keywords to drift. Generated mirrors remove that manual duplication without adding a production runtime dependency on developer tooling.
behavior_before: Run Monitor artifacts were generated together but their check was absent from shared audit suites. The config generator refreshed only the contracts schema; the PowerShell-facing schema was hand-maintained, intentionally omitted network-only fields, and had drifted to a stale DynamicHdrPolicy default annotation.
behavior_after: Config and RunMonitorRecord are documented authorities. Each generator emits both committed artifacts, applies only documented consumer metadata/projection differences, and checks every output without short-circuiting. Shared audit suites catch drift, while production Python and PowerShell validation paths remain unchanged and do not invoke developer generators.
manual_validation: 30 generator/audit/summary tests plus risky-file registry check: passed
Invoke-ReleasePackagePolicyChecks.ps1: passed; dry-run copy/exclusion plan validated

full release self-test: schema freshness, layout, release policy, tool integration, and end-to-end smoke passed; wrapper overall failed on unrelated dirty-worktree desktop tests, stale summaries, dependency/lint/doc, and WebView reliability findings
generate_config_schema --check: expected pre-regeneration mirror drift, then passed for both outputs
ruff and py_compile on scoped Python files: passed
validate_changes --require-worktree-coverage: failed only on 32 unrelated concurrent audit/generated files outside this packet
rollback_plan: Revert the two generator changes, remove the run-monitor audit registration and generator tests, restore the prior generated schema/navigation artifacts, and remove the authority documentation and risky-file entry. Runtime code and persisted settings/run-monitor state require no data rollback because their validation and storage behavior was not changed.
notes:
Pydantic Config and RunMonitorRecord remain authoritative; consumer schema files are generated artifacts. Real-media validation is not required because no media policy or runtime payload behavior is changing.
Scoped summary refresh wrote 13 schema/tool/test/doc summaries; project-index tooling rebuilt its three generated navigation outputs from the shared summary catalog.
Feature-map generation rewrote shared generated navigation outputs from the concurrently changing repository catalog; those outputs include unrelated work already present in the shared worktree.
Strict global worktree coverage is not green because concurrent repository-audit and generated-summary files are uncovered; this packet's 44 declared paths remain explicitly listed.
